intro: Port Phillip is Melbourne's home water: a big, mostly sheltered bay ringed by boat ramps from St Kilda and Black Rock round to Carrum, Mornington, Sorrento and Queenscliff, with Geelong's Corio Bay in the west. Charter boats fish the bay for snapper, King George whiting, flathead and calamari, and the bigger boats head out through the Heads into Bass Strait for gummy shark, kingfish and tuna when the weather allows.

Most Melbourne charters are shared trips of four to five hours, so you can book a single seat or the whole boat. Several operators trailer their boats and choose the ramp a few days out, depending on where the fish are, so confirm the departure point after you book.
port-phillip.season: Spring is the drawcard. Melbourne operators run their main snapper season from about October to December, with some extending it into January or April, and run three sessions a day at the peak. Whiting and calamari fish well for most of the year, gummy sharks are a cooler-season target from Queenscliff, and kingfish and tuna turn up outside the Heads from about January to early April.

p: Bay trips work the reefs, grass beds and sand flats around the edge of Port Phillip, moving with the season and the weather. Queenscliff boats sit right at the Heads, so they can fish the bay or, in good conditions, Bass Strait.

p: Victorian charter clients need their own Victorian Recreational Fishing Licence unless they are exempt; operators say it is your job to have it before the trip.
On boats crossing Port Phillip Heads, everyone must wear a life jacket through the Heads. Bag and size limits apply to snapper, whiting and calamari, so check the current VFA rules.

faq: Can I book a single seat on a Melbourne snapper charter?

Yes. Most Port Phillip operators sell individual places on shared trips as well as whole-boat charters, and some will fill the boat with other anglers. Snapper trips can need a minimum number of people to go ahead, so book early in peak season.
Which ramp will my Port Phillip charter leave from?

It often isn't fixed until a few days before. Operators such as Pro Red, Unreel and Cassar move between Carrum, St Kilda, Mornington, Hastings and other ramps to follow the fish, and confirm the meeting point after booking.
Are Port Phillip charters suitable for children?

Many are. Geelong Fishing Charters runs family trips where under-10s fish free, and bay trips generally welcome children from about five or six, but offshore Bass Strait trips usually have a minimum age of 12.

intro: Western Port lies just east of Port Phillip, wrapped around French Island and Phillip Island, with strong tidal currents and deep channels. Hastings is the charter hub, with boats leaving the Hastings boat ramp and Western Port Marina, and Stony Point and Corinella also used. The bay is known for big spring snapper, King George whiting, and gummy sharks in the channels.

Hastings is also the main launch for Melbourne's offshore trips into Bass Strait, where charters chase kingfish, southern bluefin tuna and mako sharks. Boats range from trailered catamarans for six to eight anglers to a 15 metre vessel that takes groups of up to 20.
western-port.season: Snapper move into Western Port in spring, and operators fish them from about September or October, with Hastings often firing early in the season before the run moves into Port Phillip. Whiting is reliable for much of the year, best from about October to May. Gummy sharks are caught year-round, and offshore kingfish and tuna trips run mostly from summer into autumn.

p: Tides drive the fishing here: skippers time trips around the tide changes and fish the channels and banks around the islands.

p: Offshore Bass Strait trips are weather dependent and often have a minimum age of 12; bay trips suit families. Bring your own Victorian fishing licence, as most operators don't sell them on board.

faq: Is Western Port or Port Phillip better for snapper?

Both get a spring run. Several operators start the season at Hastings in Western Port and shift to Port Phillip ramps such as Carrum as the run moves up the bay, choosing a few days out based on where fish are biting.
Can I go offshore into Bass Strait from Hastings?

Yes. Hastings is the usual departure for offshore trips targeting kingfish, southern bluefin tuna and sharks. Trips run up to about eight hours, depend on the weather, and usually have a minimum age of 12.

intro: Portland, in Victoria's far south-west, is the state's best-known southern bluefin tuna port. Nutrient-rich water from the Bonney Upwelling and a short run to deep water bring tuna, sharks and big reef fish within reach, and in autumn and winter many Melbourne charter boats join the local fleet. Port Fairy, about an hour east, is the other main base.

Local skippers fish all year, bottom-bouncing for snapper, gummy shark, flathead and nannygai and deep-dropping on the shelf, while tuna days are long, often eight to ten hours. Expect a full day offshore and pack for cold, rough conditions.
portland.season: Bluefin tuna are the main event from about March to August. Local Portland operators quote May to August for tuna trips, Melbourne operators list school fish from about April to July and big 'barrel' fish from March to October, and some run Portland trips from May to September. Kingfish are a summer target, especially around Port Fairy, and reef fishing runs all year.

p: Southern bluefin tuna have a daily bag limit, and VFA officers check that recreational and charter anglers stick to it, so check the current VFA rules before you go. Tuna trips can mean a long run offshore, so take seasickness tablets beforehand if you need them.

faq: How far offshore do Portland tuna charters go?
Often a long way. Bluefin are frequently found well offshore, sometimes over the continental shelf, so tuna charters are usually full days of about eight to ten hours.
Do Melbourne charter operators fish Portland?
Yes. Several Melbourne operators, including Pro Red, Unreel, Cassar and Sharkmen, run seasonal bluefin tuna trips out of Portland, alongside local Portland and Port Fairy boats.
Is Port Fairy a good alternative to Portland?
Yes. Port Fairy has its own charter boats that chase tuna, sharks and kingfish, and some will launch from Portland or Warrnambool depending on the weather and where the fish are.

intro: Lakes Entrance sits where the Gippsland Lakes meet Bass Strait, and it is the jumping-off point for East Gippsland's offshore fishing. Charter boats cross the bar from the Skate Park ramp to grounds about 20 to 40 minutes out, targeting snapper, gummy shark and flathead, with sharks and game fish further offshore.

Behind the entrance, the Gippsland Lakes are one of Victoria's best bream fisheries, with big dusky flathead from the entrance up to Metung and Paynesville. Some Lakes Entrance operators also run crabbing and lake trips, so ask what is running when you visit.
gippsland.season: Snapper are caught off Lakes Entrance all year, with pinkies arriving in numbers from about May and some of the state's biggest snapper landed between October and April. Gummy sharks build as the water warms towards summer. In the lakes, bream and flathead fish well through the warmer months, and crabbing is best from about October to January.

p: The Lakes Entrance bar can be dangerous, with strong tides, so skippers time crossings around conditions and trips are weather dependent. Health advice on eating whole fish from the Gippsland Lakes has applied in recent years, so check the current advice before keeping lake fish.

faq: Do Lakes Entrance charters fish the lakes or the ocean?
Mostly the ocean. Far Out Charters fishes offshore in Bass Strait for snapper, gummy shark and flathead; lake fishing and crabbing trips are run by some other local operators.
How long is the run to the fishing grounds from Lakes Entrance?
Usually short. Far Out Charters says most trips take about 20 to 40 minutes to reach the grounds after crossing the bar.

intro: The Murray forms Victoria's northern border and is the heartland of Murray cod fishing. Lake Mulwala, created by Yarrawonga Weir, is one of the country's top cod fisheries, where fish breed naturally among the drowned timber of the old river bed, and the river downstream towards Echuca and Swan Hill also holds big cod.

Guided trips are small-boat lure fishing for one to three anglers, using surface lures, swimbaits and modern sonar to find fish. Lake Mulwala and the Murray itself are New South Wales waters, so check which licence and rules apply before you fish.
murray-river.season: Murray cod can be fished from December to August. The closed season runs from 1 September to 30 November, and the river from Yarrawonga Weir to Tocumwal is closed to all fishing during that time. Summer mornings and evenings suit active fish, winter is the time for trophy cod, and golden perch are a good target in spring.

p: Lake Mulwala is NSW water, so a NSW recreational fishing licence applies there; Lake Mulwala Sportfishing includes the licence in its prices. Size and bag limits for Murray cod differ between waters, so check the current NSW DPI or VFA rules. Most guides practise catch and release on big cod.

faq: Is Lake Mulwala in Victoria or New South Wales?
The lake sits between Yarrawonga in Victoria and Mulwala in NSW, but it is classified as NSW water, so a NSW recreational fishing licence applies whether you fish from a boat, kayak or the shore.
Can I fish for Murray cod in spring?

Not for cod in most waters: the closed season runs 1 September to 30 November, and the Murray from Yarrawonga Weir to Tocumwal is closed to all fishing then. Guides switch to golden perch during the closure.

intro: Lake Eildon and the High Country around Mansfield combine a big lake known for trophy Murray cod and golden perch with some of Victoria's most scenic trout streams. Rivers such as the Delatite, Howqua, Jamieson, King and upper Goulburn are fished on foot by fly anglers, while larger tailrace rivers suit drift boats.
Guiding here is usually one guide to one or two anglers, with waders and fly gear supplied, and guided river fishing is mostly catch and release.
eildon.season: Lake Eildon has no Murray cod closed season, so cod can be chased all year there, though more are caught in the warmer months. In rivers, cod follow the statewide closure from 1 September to 30 November, and guided cod drift trips run December to April. Trout rivers have their own season, so check the current VFA rules before planning a river trip.

items: Trophy Murray cod and golden perch
December to August; guided drift trips December to April

p: Many High Country rivers have no mobile reception, so guides give indicative pick-up and return times and carry satellite messengers. Anglers 18 to 69 need a Victorian Recreational Fishing Licence unless exempt.

faq: Do I need fly-fishing experience for a guided High Country trip?
No. Guides take first-timers through to experienced anglers, with tuition included and waders, boots, rods and flies supplied.
Is there phone reception on High Country rivers?
Often not. Back of Beyond Fly Fishing notes most locations have no mobile coverage, gives indicative pick-up and drop-off times, and carries a satellite messenger with SOS.

intro: Victoria packs a lot of fishing into a small state. Melbourne's two bays, Port Phillip and Western Port, are famous for the spring snapper run and King George whiting, while Bass Strait offers sharks, kingfish and tuna. Portland in the far south-west is the bluefin tuna capital, Lakes Entrance opens onto East Gippsland's reefs and lakes, and inland the Murray and Lake Eildon are Murray cod country.
victoria.season: Spring (October to December) is snapper season in Melbourne's bays, summer brings kingfish and mako sharks, and autumn into winter is bluefin tuna time at Portland and Port Fairy. Murray cod are closed from 1 September to 30 November in most waters, but Lake Eildon stays open all year.

p: Unless exempt, anglers must hold a Victorian Recreational Fishing Licence, including on charter boats; exemptions cover people under 18 or 70 and over, certain concession card holders, and Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people. Lake Mulwala and the Murray are NSW waters, where NSW rules apply. Bag and size limits change, so check the current VFA rules.

faq: Which part of Victoria should I base a fishing charter trip in?

It depends on the target. Melbourne's bays suit snapper, whiting and family trips close to the city; Portland and Port Fairy are the bases for bluefin tuna; Lakes Entrance offers offshore reef fishing; and Yarrawonga and Mansfield are the bases for guided Murray cod and trout.
